To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

death-related cognition decreased satisfaction with life and subjective vitality, meaning, and exploration, increased negative affect and social avoidance, and exacerbated state anxiety, for individuals with low but not high self-esteem.
mortality salience decreases satisfaction with life, meaning in life and exploration and increases negative affect and state anxiousness for individuals with low, but not high, self-esteem.

low self-esteem individuals who are reminded of their own mortality are less satisfied with life, less vital, less motivated to grow, less likely to engage in exploratory behavior, more anxious, more likely to experience negative affect, more likely to avoid others, and less likely to experience positive affect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of mortality awareness and self-esteem on well-being, growth, and maladaptive behaviors.
the ways in which the awareness of death can affect the psychological functioning of individuals who have different levels of self-esteem.

the ways in which the human need to manage death anxiety affects psychological functioning and maladaptive behavior, and the ways in which self-esteem influences the relationship between death-related cognition and psychological adjustment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of mortality on well-being are mediated by self-esteem.
death-related cognition decreases psychological adjustment, but only for people with low self-esteem.
the effects of death-related cognition on psychological well-being and maladaptive behavior are mediated by self-esteem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
self-esteem is a critical moderator of the effects of death cognition on adjustment.
self-esteem and death cognition have independent and interactive effects on psychological adjustment.
death-related thoughts are a potent threat to the psychological adjustment of individuals with low self-worth, but not to those who have a strong sense of self-esteem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
death-related cognition can be a source of maladaptive behavior, especially for individuals with low levels of self-esteem.
self-esteem and death cognition interact in a manner that affects psychological adjustment.
death cognition can be harmful to psychological well-being, but this harm is buffered by self-esteem.
